name: Planning Poker
highLevelGoals: The Moderator aims to efficiently create, configure, and manage Planning Poker game sessions, including adding, editing, and deleting items for estimation, to streamline the sprint goal setting process.

The Moderator seeks to accurately finalize estimates for stories, whether by accepting an average, automatically filling in consensus estimates, or manually entering an agreed-upon value, to ensure clear sprint commitments.

The Moderator desires to access and export comprehensive game transcripts and historical data in various formats (HTML, CSV) to maintain records, analyze past estimations, and support future planning.

The Moderator aims to have full control over their account, including creation, login, modification of details, and secure deletion, to manage their personal information and access to the application effectively.
The Moderator wants to configure game settings such as estimation scales and the number of participants to tailor the Planning Poker experience to their team's specific needs and preferences.
The Estimator aims to seamlessly join a Planning Poker game and actively participate by submitting estimates for stories, ensuring their input is captured effectively.
The Estimator seeks to be well-informed during the estimation process by viewing the current item, all items for the session, and prior estimates, to make accurate and considered judgments.
The Estimator desires the ability to change their estimate during a round, up until all cards are revealed, to reflect evolving understanding and discussion outcomes.

The Participant aims for transparency in the estimation process, including seeing who has estimated, receiving immediate notifications of estimates, and viewing prior estimates, to foster open discussion and understanding.
The Participant wants the ability to initiate and manage a countdown timer to ensure discussions remain focused and time-bound, promoting efficient decision-making.
The Participant desires a consistent and predictable user experience, including consistent card order and personalized elements like thumbnail photos, to enhance usability and engagement.

The Developer aims to build an application that is broadly accessible and compatible across various browsers and devices, adhering to web standards (XHTML, CSS, W3C accessibility) to maximize user reach.
The Developer seeks to ensure the application performs optimally with fast response times and efficient database operations (e.g., through indexing) to provide a smooth and engaging user experience.
The Developer aims to create a robust system with user-friendly error pages and sensible URLs, fostering user trust and making the application intuitive and reliable.
The Researcher aims to collect game results in a non-identifiable manner to conduct studies on estimation patterns and team dynamics while upholding privacy and ethical data practices.
lowLevelGoals: The Moderator can initiate a new game session within the application.
The Moderator can adjust parameters for the current game session, such as estimation scale and participant limits.
The Moderator can input a new story or task that needs to be estimated by the team.
The Moderator can modify the details of a story or task that has already been added for estimation.
The Moderator can remove a story or task from the list of items to be estimated.
The Moderator can choose to finalize a story's estimate by accepting the calculated average of all submitted estimates.
The Moderator can trigger the system to automatically set the estimate for a story based on a predefined consensus rule.
The Moderator can input a specific numerical value as the final estimate for a story, overriding any calculated averages or consensus.
The Moderator can retrieve and view the detailed record of a previously completed Planning Poker game.
The Moderator can download the full game transcript as an HTML file for easy viewing in a web browser.
The Moderator can download the full game transcript as a CSV file for data analysis in spreadsheet software.
The Moderator can register for a new user account within the application.
The Moderator can authenticate and gain access to their existing account.
The Moderator can update their profile information, such as name, email, or password.
The Moderator can permanently remove their account and associated data from the system.
The Moderator can select from predefined estimation scales (e.g., Fibonacci, T-shirt sizes) or define a custom one for the game.
The Moderator can specify how many estimators are allowed to join a particular game.
The Estimator can enter a game session, typically using a unique game ID or link.
The Estimator can select and submit their chosen estimate value for the story being discussed.
The Estimator can see the description and any relevant information for the story currently being estimated.
The Estimator can see a list of all stories or tasks that will be estimated during the game session.
The Estimator can access the finalized estimates for stories that have already been completed in the session.
The Estimator can modify their chosen estimate for the current story as long as the moderator has not yet revealed all estimates.
The Participant can see a visual indicator or list of who has already cast their vote for the current story.
The Participant gets real-time alerts when another participant submits their estimate.
The Participant can access the finalized estimates for stories that have already been estimated in the session.
The Participant can start a timer to manage the duration of discussions for a story.
The Participant can set the length of the discussion timer.
The system should display estimation cards in the same sequence for all participants.
The system should show small profile pictures for each participant to enhance recognition and engagement.
The Developer must implement the application to function correctly across popular web browsers (e.g., Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari).
The Developer must design and implement the user interface to adapt and display correctly on different screen sizes (e.g., desktop, tablet, mobile).
The Developer must ensure all HTML markup conforms to XHTML specifications for structural integrity and compatibility.
The Developer must ensure all styling adheres to CSS specifications for consistent presentation and maintainability.
The Developer must implement features and design choices that comply with W3C accessibility standards to ensure usability for individuals with disabilities.
The Developer must implement techniques to minimize the time taken for the application to respond to user interactions.
The Developer must create and manage database indexes to speed up data retrieval and manipulation queries.
The Developer must design and implement custom error pages that provide clear, helpful information to users when an error occurs.
The Developer must design the application's URL structure to be logical, readable, and easy to understand for users.
The Researcher can access game data where all personal information of participants has been anonymized or removed.
